conventions: TypeScript strict mode; no `any` in new code; no new dependencies.
Formatting is Prettier via eslint-plugin-prettier (@excalidraw/prettier-config): 80 columns, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas, 2-space indent; `eslint --fix` applies it.
Import order as in EyeDropper.tsx: external packages, then @excalidraw/* value imports, blank line, `import type` lines, blank line, relative imports.
Internal packages are imported by their aliases (`@excalidraw/common`, `@excalidraw/element`, `@excalidraw/math`), never by relative paths across packages.
Tests run on Vitest with globals (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi`, `afterEach` are not imported) and jest-style matchers (`toBe`, `toEqual`).
Editor tests render `<Excalidraw />` through `render` from ./test-utils, seed elements with `API.createElement` + `h.app.updateScene` inside `act`, and read state via `const { h } = window;`.
Colour hex strings are lowercase, as produced by `rgbToHex`; compare colours as strings with `toBe`.
Keep comments to one short line where the intent is not obvious; no commented-out code.

decisions.topic: Name and signature of the dark-mode inverse (FR-4)
decisions.choice: `export const reverseDarkModeFilter = (color: string): string` in packages/common/src/colors.ts, placed right after `applyDarkModeFilter`, re-exported by the existing `export * from "./colors"`; it keeps the input's alpha the way `applyDarkModeFilter` does (6-digit hex when opaque, 8-digit otherwise) and returns an invalid input unchanged.
rejected: invertDarkModeFilter (clashes with the private cssInvert step)
an (r, g, b) number signature (callers hold hex strings)
decisions.reason: Mirrors applyDarkModeFilter's string-in/string-out contract so callers compose the two directly.

decisions.topic: How the inverse finds a pre-image
decisions.choice: No search: the 180-degree hue matrix is M = 2W - I (its own inverse), so every output channel is u_i = 2L - v_i with L the luminance of the invert-space point v (integers 18..237); for pixel (r, g, b) the canonical pre-image is vG = Math.round(0.426r + 0.43g + 0.144b), vR = vG + g - r, vB = vG + g - b, each clamped to 18..237; the inverse runs cssHueRotate on that centre, then on its other 26 +/-1 neighbours to absorb floating-point ties at .5, returns the first exact match (else the nearest), and maps v back to light space with a one-time 256-entry cssInvert table. Bound per call: at most 27 cssHueRotate evaluations, zero applyDarkModeFilter calls, no result cache.
rejected: the earlier phase-2 sweep over (vR, vB) for clamped pixels (up to ~145k candidate evaluations per call, breaks NFR-3)
a result cache as the cost bound (a cold call is still unbounded)
closed-form inverse without verification (a .5 tie can flip one rounding)
precomputing a full reverse table (16M forward evaluations)
decisions.reason: Green never clamps and u_i - uG = vG - v_i is an integer, so an unclamped pixel has exactly one pre-image, round(M x pixel); a red or blue channel clamped at 0 or 255 only bounds vG - v_i from one side, and the canonical point sits on that bound, which case by case (one channel high or low, both high, both low; mixed high/low has no pre-image) is a pre-image whenever any exists, so FR-4 holds for every colour at fixed cost.

decisions.choice: Each eyedropper pointermove does one topmost-element hit-test walk, at most 3 applyDarkModeFilter calls (background, stroke, view background) and at most one reverseDarkModeFilter call, which itself does at most 27 cssHueRotate evaluations; none of these counts depends on the colour.
rejected: bounding cost by memoising inverse results (a cache does not bound a cold call)
decisions.reason: NFR-3 caps per-move work at one hit-test, a constant number of filter calls and one constant-cost inverse.

decisions.topic: Where the exact stored colour comes from (FR-1)
decisions.choice: In dark theme the eyedropper hit-tests the topmost element at the cursor and returns the first stored candidate whose `applyDarkModeFilter` equals the sampled pixel, in this order: that element's backgroundColor, its strokeColor, then `app.state.viewBackgroundColor`; only when none matches does it return `reverseDarkModeFilter(pixel)` (FR-2).
rejected: inverse only (the filter is not injective, so it cannot return the stored hex for colliding colours)
matching against every element in the scene (unbounded per-move cost)
decisions.reason: The scene is the only source that can return the stored value byte for byte, at a constant three filter calls per move.

decisions.choice: Loop `app.scene.getNonDeletedElements()` from the last index down and take the first element for which `hitElementItself` (from @excalidraw/element) is true, with threshold `element.strokeWidth / 2 + 0.1` and `elementsMap: app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap()`.
rejected: App.getElementAtPosition (not on AppClassProperties, and packages/excalidraw/types.ts is outside the allowlist)
decisions.reason: Uses only what `useApp()` exposes and keeps the change inside the frozen allowlist.

decisions.choice: The swatch background shows the on-screen pixel colour; `onChange` and `onSelect` receive the picked colour.
rejected: showing the picked (light-theme) colour, which would not match what the user sees under the cursor in dark theme
decisions.reason: The swatch mirrors the canvas the user is looking at; the callbacks carry the value that is stored.

decisions.topic: Theme and coordinates source in the eyedropper
decisions.choice: Read `stableProps.app.state` at event time for theme, zoom, scroll and viewBackgroundColor; keep the existing `appState.offsetLeft/offsetTop` pixel read unchanged; the effect's dependency list does not change.
rejected: adding appState.theme to the effect dependencies (re-attaches listeners on theme change for no gain)
decisions.reason: app.state is always current and UIAppState omits zoom and scroll.

decisions.topic: How the eyedropper test controls the sampled pixel
decisions.choice: Before pressing `i`, take `const ctx = h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!`, `vi.spyOn(ctx, "getImageData")` to return `{ data: Uint8ClampedArray.of(r, g, b, 255) } as ImageData`, and `vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas, "getContext").mockReturnValue(ctx)`; restore with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in afterEach.
rejected: spying CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype (the canvas mock defines its methods per instance)
decisions.reason: jsdom's canvas mock does not render, and pinning getContext makes the stub hold whether or not the mock caches contexts.

units.behaviour: Adds a `reverseDarkModeFilter` describe block with round-trip tests that fail until the inverse helper exists.
rules: 1. Import `reverseDarkModeFilter` alongside the existing named imports from "@excalidraw/common" (order: applyDarkModeFilter, COLOR_PALETTE, reverseDarkModeFilter, rgbToHex).

2. Inside the new describe, define `const roundTripFailures = (colors: string[]) => colors.filter((c) => applyDarkModeFilter(reverseDarkModeFilter(applyDarkModeFilter(c))) !== applyDarkModeFilter(c));` and assert each round-trip case with `expect(roundTripFailures(list)).toEqual([])` so a failure lists the offending colours.
3. The palette list is `Object.values(COLOR_PALETTE).flat()` with "transparent" removed.
4. The saturated list is exactly ["#ff00ff", "#00ff00", "#0000ff", "#ff0000", "#000000", "#ffffff"].
5. The cube sample is every rgbToHex(r, g, b) with r, g and b each stepping from 0 to 255 by 15 (18 levels, 5832 colours, both faces 0 and 255 included), built with nested loops.
6. The injective case asserts `reverseDarkModeFilter(applyDarkModeFilter(c))` toBe c for each of "#000000", "#808080", "#ffffff" (each grey level has a single pre-image under the filter).

7. The cache case first calls reverseDarkModeFilter on "#ff9090", "#ededed" and "#ff70ff", then asserts applyDarkModeFilter("#ff0000") toBe "#ff9090", applyDarkModeFilter("#000000") toBe "#ededed" and applyDarkModeFilter("#ff00ff") toBe "#ff70ff".
8. No snapshot is used; the snapshot file is not touched.

rules: 1. Add imports: `THEME`, `applyDarkModeFilter` from "@excalidraw/common"; `CaptureUpdateAction` from "@excalidraw/element"; `API` from "./helpers/api"; `act` added to the existing ./test-utils import.
2. The new top-level describe is named "eye dropper picked color" and starts with `const { h } = window;` and `afterEach(() => { vi.restoreAllMocks(); });`.

3. A local helper `pickAt(stored: string)`, used by both cases: seed `API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 20, y: 20, width: 120, height: 100, backgroundColor: stored, fillStyle: "solid", strokeColor: "#1e1e1e", roundness: null })` via `act(() => h.app.updateScene({ elements: [rect], captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }))`.

4. In pickAt, derive the pixel bytes by parsing `applyDarkModeFilter(stored)` hex pairs with `parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16)`; take `const ctx = h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!`, `vi.spyOn(ctx, "getImageData").mockReturnValue({ data: Uint8ClampedArray.of(r, g, b, 255) } as ImageData)` and `vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas, "getContext").mockReturnValue(ctx)`, all before the key press.

5. In pickAt, then `Keyboard.keyPress("i")`, `await waitFor` until `.excalidraw-eye-dropper-backdrop` exists in GlobalTestState.renderResult.container, and fire `fireEvent.pointerDown` then `fireEvent.pointerUp` on that backdrop, both with `{ clientX: 80, clientY: 70 }` (scene point 80,70 is inside the rectangle).
6. The dark case renders `<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} theme={THEME.DARK} />`; the light case renders the same without `theme`.
7. Each case asserts with `await waitFor(() => expect(h.state.currentItemBackgroundColor).toBe(expected))`.
8. The dark case name contains "dark theme" and the light case name must not, so the red check filter selects only the dark case.

units.behaviour: Adds `reverseDarkModeFilter`, which maps a dark-mode rendered colour to a light-theme colour that renders back to it, exact where the filter is injective.
rules: 1. No result cache of any kind: reverseDarkModeFilter is pure and does the same bounded work on every call.

2. A private lazily built `number[]` table maps each invert-space value v to the smallest x in 0..255 with `cssInvert(x, x, x, 93).r === v`, filled once on first use by iterating x from 0 to 255; V_MIN is `cssInvert(255, 255, 255, 93).r` (18) and V_MAX is `cssInvert(0, 0, 0, 93).r` (237).
3. `reverseDarkModeFilter(color)`: `const tc = tinycolor(color)`; if `!tc.isValid()` return `color`; read `{ r, g, b }` from `tc.toRgb()` and `alpha` from `tc.getAlpha()`.

4. Canonical centre, solved from the hue matrix's linear relations (no search): `const vG0 = Math.round(0.426 * r + 0.43 * g + 0.144 * b)`, then `vR0 = vG0 + g - r` and `vB0 = vG0 + g - b` as exact integer offsets (never rounded separately); clamp each of the three to [V_MIN, V_MAX] with `clamp`.

5. Candidates, in this order: the centre first, then the other 26 points of its +/-1 neighbourhood looping dR, dG, dB each over -1, 0, 1 (red outermost, centre skipped); skip a candidate with any coordinate outside [V_MIN, V_MAX]; for each, `const out = cssHueRotate(vR, vG, vB, 180 as Degrees)`.
6. Return at the first candidate whose out equals (r, g, b); otherwise use the candidate with the smallest squared distance between out and (r, g, b), the earlier one winning ties.

7. Bound (NFR-3): at most 27 cssHueRotate evaluations per call and no other loop over colour space; there is no fallback sweep, the result for clamped pixels (a 0 or 255 red or blue channel) comes from the same centre and neighbourhood.
8. The result is `rgbToHex(table[vR], table[vG], table[vB], alpha)` for the chosen candidate.
9. Never call applyDarkModeFilter and never read or write DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE; cssInvert, cssHueRotate and applyDarkModeFilter stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

10. A short JSDoc above the export states the round-trip guarantee `applyDarkModeFilter(reverseDarkModeFilter(applyDarkModeFilter(c))) === applyDarkModeFilter(c)` and that the work is at most 27 hue-rotate evaluations.

units.behaviour: In dark theme the eyedropper returns the stored scene colour that renders to the sampled pixel, falling back to reverseDarkModeFilter; light theme is unchanged and the swatch keeps showing the on-screen pixel.
rules: 1. `getCurrentColor` returns `{ screenColor: string; pickedColor: string }`; screenColor is `rgbToHex(pixel[0], pixel[1], pixel[2])` read exactly as today.
2. `const { app } = stableProps;` if `app.state.theme !== THEME.DARK`, return `{ screenColor, pickedColor: screenColor }`.
3. Otherwise get `{ x, y }` from `viewportCoordsToSceneCoords({ clientX, clientY }, app.state)` and `const elementsMap = app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap()`.

4. Find the topmost hit: walk `app.scene.getNonDeletedElements()` from the last index down and stop at the first element for which `hitElementItself({ point: pointFrom(x, y), element, threshold: element.strokeWidth / 2 + 0.1, elementsMap })` is true.
5. Candidates in order: the hit element's backgroundColor, its strokeColor (both only when an element was hit), then `app.state.viewBackgroundColor`.

6. pickedColor is the first candidate whose `applyDarkModeFilter(candidate)` equals screenColor, returned as stored; when none matches it is `reverseDarkModeFilter(screenColor)`, called at most once per event and never memoised here (its own cost is bounded by U03).

7. The pointermove handler passes pickedColor to `stableProps.onChange` and sets `colorPreviewDiv.style.background` to screenColor; the pointerup handler passes `getCurrentColor(event).pickedColor` to onSelect.
8. The effect's dependency array, listeners and preview positioning are unchanged.
